newsitem.title: USA: US debt futures end sharply lower, unable to bounce.
newsitem.headline: US debt futures end sharply lower, unable to bounce.

text.p: U.S. debt futures finished sharply lower, unable to bounce off lows which were set earlier after a senior Federal Reserve official said eight out of 12 Fed banks requested a hike in the U.S. discount rate.

While most traders said the official's comments were not that surprising given that the market was looking for a rate hike less than two weeks ago, they said the inability for December T-bond USZ6 to rebound from a strong knee-jerk reaction to the comments could indicate further declines.
"Bonds keep finding offers everytime they want to bounce," one bond futures floor source said."
In fact, December T-bond set a daily low of 108-01/32 in the final hour of trade.
"I'm not so sure those comments are so new, but the fact the market couldn't bounce at all is troubling," another floor trader said.

The Fed source told Reuters that three out of the eight Fed banks were calling for a 50-basis-point hike in the discount rate, and that the Fed consensus is centered around a 25-basis-point hike in the fed funds rate on September 24.
"I'm amazed the Fed would make that public," one analyst said.
"The political momentum must be to leave well enough alone, but some must be objecting to that," he said.

Another analyst said the comments appeared because the market was still holding Friday's gains, despite Federal Reserve governor Lawrence Lindsey's statements on Friday afternoon that he sees rising U.S. inflation risks.
"The reason we saw the comment leaked to the press is because the market still didn't break after Lindsey's comments late Friday," he said.
The Fed comments on Tuesday shocked the market, which had just recovered from the production and utilization data.

Industrial production rose 0.5 percent and capacity utilization climbed to 83.5, both higher than had been expected. December T-bonds immediately fell to 108-16/32, while December Eurodollars eased to 94.12.
However, the losses were short-lived as locals, in particular, covered positions and turned long.
"Locals got shellacked when the Fed comments came out," one floor source said. "They were on the wrong side of the market when the numbers came out and then they were long when the market tanked."
One pit trader said the downmove was "ugly."
"I want my mother," he said, sitting on the sidelines in quiet midday trade. "It got really ugly in there. Ugly."

December bonds closed below support at 108-11/32, which weakens the market's near-term outlook, traders said. They noted that before the comments were released, December still failed to test Friday's three-week high at 109-00.

At the end of pit trade, December T-bonds were down 22/32 at 108-04/32, 10-year notes were off 16/32 at 106-18, December Eurodollars were off eight bps at 94.07, March Euros were down 10 bps at 93.91, March T-bills were down 11 bps at 94.48.
